record.paper_title: Open Problems Related to Quantum Query Complexity
record.original_question: For every n-qubit unitary transformation U, does there exist a Boolean oracle A:{0,1}*->{0,1} such that a BQP^A machine can implement U?

evidence.quote: In 2007, Greg Kuperberg and I [8] raised the following question:
Problem 6 For every n-qubit unitary transformation U, does there exist an oracle A :{0, 1}∗→ {0, 1} such that a BQPA machine can implement U?
In my 2016 Barbados lecture notes [4], I took to calling this the “Unitary Synthesis Problem.” It remains wide open.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let BQP^A denote the class of problems (and more generally, transformations) implementable by a polynomial-time quantum Turing machine with oracle access to a Boolean function A:{0,1}*→{0,1}. The Unitary Synthesis Problem asks:

Does there exist, for every positive integer n and every n-qubit unitary transformation U acting on (C^2)^{⊗n}, a Boolean oracle A:{0,1}*→{0,1} such that a BQP^A machine, on input n and a description of the desired precision ε>0, implements U (to within error ε in operator norm) using time polynomial in n and 1/ε?

Equivalently: can the task of implementing an arbitrary n-qubit unitary be efficiently reduced, via an oracle quantum polynomial-time algorithm, to the task of computing some classical Boolean function?
artifact.status_search_result: The full problem remains open. Lombardi, Ma, and Wright (STOC 2024, arXiv:2310.08870) proved a one-query lower bound: there exist unitaries that cannot be implemented (even approximately) by any polynomial-time quantum algorithm making a single query to a Boolean oracle. A 2025 follow-up (arXiv:2508.13215) extends this to a 1.5-query lower bound. No general lower bound for arbitrarily many queries is known, so the original Aaronson–Kuperberg question is still unresolved.

status_evidence.title: A One-Query Lower Bound for Unitary Synthesis and Breaking Quantum Cryptography
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes the first general one-query lower bound for the Unitary Synthesis Problem, showing some unitaries cannot be implemented with a single oracle query.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress: one-query lower bound proven, but general problem unresolved.

status_evidence.title: A 1.5-Query Lower Bound for the Unitary Synthesis Problem
status_evidence.snippet: Extends the lower bound to 1.5 queries, indicating the problem remains open beyond small query counts.
status_evidence.claim: Further partial progress; full problem still open.

status_evidence.title: Open Problems Related to Quantum Query Complexity
status_evidence.snippet: Aaronson states the Unitary Synthesis Problem 'remains wide open.'
